chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Fulan al-Waqifi, who said:

There was a cousin of mine called Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah; he was an ascetic and was among the most devout worshippers of his time. The ruler used to hold him in awe because of his seriousness in religion and his striving; sometimes he would confront the ruler with harsh words, admonishing him, commanding him to good, and forbidding him from evil. The ruler would endure him because of his righteousness. This remained his state until one day Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) came to him while he was in the mosque.

He (the Imam) saw him and gestured to him; he came to him. He said to him: 'O Abu Ali! How beloved to me is what you are engaged in, and how it pleases me — except that you have no ma'rifa. So seek the ma'rifa.' He said: 'May I be your ransom! What is ma'rifa?' He said: 'Go and acquire jurisprudential knowledge and seek hadith.' He said: 'From whom?' He said: 'From the jurists of the people of Medina; then present the hadith to me.'

He said: So he went and wrote (them) down, then came to him and recited them. He (the Imam) rejected all of it, then said to him: 'Go and attain the true ma'rifa.' The man was deeply concerned about his religion; he did not cease to watch for Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) until he (the Imam) went out to his estate; he met him on the road. He said to him: 'May I be your ransom! I will argue before God with you — guide me to ma'rifa.'

He said: So he (the Imam) informed him about the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and what happened after the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and informed him about the matter of the two men (Abu Bakr and Umar). He accepted this from him. Then he said to him: 'Who was after the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him)?' He said: 'Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), then Al-Husayn (peace be upon him),' until he reached himself; then he fell silent. He said: He then said to him: 'May I be your ransom! Who is the Imam today?' He said: 'If I inform you, will you accept?' He said: 'Yes, may I be your ransom!' He said: 'I am he.'

He said: 'Is there something I can use as evidence?' He (the Imam) said: 'Go to that tree,' — and he gestured with his hand toward the Umm Ghaylan (a type of acacia tree) — 'and say to it: Musa ibn Ja'far commands you to come forward.' He said: So I went to it and, I swear by God, I saw it plowing through the earth until it stopped before him. Then he gestured to it and it returned. He said: He acknowledged him and thereafter devoted himself to silence and worship; no one saw him speak after that.
Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim — similar to it.

key_terms.أُمُّ غَيْلَانَ: Umm Ghaylan — a type of acacia tree (Faidherbia albida), used here as a miraculous sign confirming the Imam's authority
key_terms.الْأَمْرُ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَالنَّهْيُ عَن: Enjoining good and forbidding evil — the Islamic obligation of moral accountability in society
key_terms.الْوَاقِفِيّ: Waqifi — member of the Waqifiyya sect who believed the Imamate ended with Imam Musa al-Kazim
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: A phrase of deep reverence meaning 'may I be sacrificed/ransomed for you', used as a form of address to the Imam
key_terms.مَعْرِفَة: Gnosis, recognition — specifically the recognition of the rightful Imam as a spiritual and religious obligation

ai.seo_question: What miracle did Imam Musa al-Kazim perform to prove his Imamate to a devout ascetic?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates how Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) guided a devout but misguided cousin of his narrator, Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah, toward the true gnosis (ma'rifa) of the Imamate. Despite Al-Hasan's exceptional piety and his practice of enjoining good and forbidding evil even toward the ruler, the Imam recognized that outward worship without recognition of the rightful Imam was spiritually incomplete. The Imam first directed him to study hadith from Medinan jurists — deliberately leading him to a dead end — and only when Al-Hasan persisted did the Imam reveal the chain of Imams culminating in himself, and confirmed his Imamate by miraculously commanding an acacia tree to uproot itself and walk to him. Al-Hasan's subsequent embrace of silence and devoted worship indicates the profundity of his conversion. The narrator is identified as a Waqifi — one who believed the Imamate ended with the seventh Imam — making this account particularly striking as self-testimony about the eighth Imam's authority.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Fulan the Waqifiite who said,

‘There was a cousin of mine called Al-Hassan Bin Abdullah who was ascetic, and he was from the most devout worshippers of his time, and the ruler used to fear him due to his devoutness in the Religion and his striving, and sometimes he used to face the ruler with harsh speech advising him and instructing him with the goodness and forbidding him from the evil, and it was so that the ruler used to endure him due to his righteousness. And this did not cease to be his state until it was from the days when he went over to Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> was in the Masjid.

So he<sup>asws</sup> saw him and gestured towards him and said to him: ‘O Abu Ali! How beloved it is to me<sup>asws</sup> what you are in and it cheers me<sup>asws</sup> except that there isn’t any ‘مَعْرِفَة’ understanding for you. Therefore, seek the understanding’. He said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! And what is the understanding?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Go and ponder and seek the Hadeeth’. He said, ‘From whom?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘عَنْ فُقَهَاءِ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ’ ‘From the jurists of the people of Al Medina, then present the Hadeeth unto me<sup>asws</sup>’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So he went, and wrote down (the Ahadeeth), then came over with it and recited it to him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> rejected all of it, then said to him: ‘Go and recognise the understanding’. And he was the man serious with his Religion, so he did not cease to hang around Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> until he<sup>asws</sup> went out to a property of his<sup>asws</sup>, so he met him<sup>asws</sup> in the road. So he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I want to argue against you<sup>asws</sup> in front of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so indicate me upon ‘الْمَعْرِفَةِ’ the recognition’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> informed him of Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> and what had occurred after Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and informed him of the matter of the two men (Abu Bakr and Umar). So he accepted from him<sup>asws</sup>, then said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So who was after Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, then Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>’, until he<sup>asws</sup> ended up to himself<sup>asws</sup>. Then he<sup>asws</sup> was silent. So he said, ‘So who is he (the Imam<sup>asws</sup>) today?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If I<sup>asws</sup> inform you, will you accept?’ He Said, ‘Yes, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>!’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> am he<sup>asws</sup>’.

He said: ‘So is there anything to evidence with it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Go to that tree’, and he<sup>asws</sup> gestured towards Umm Gaylan (a type of tree), ‘and say to it, ‘Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> is telling you, ‘come to me’. He said, ‘So I went over to it and said it. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, it furrowed the ground with a furrowing until it stopped in front of him<sup>asws</sup>. Then he<sup>asws</sup> gestured towards it, so it returned. So he acknowledged with it, the necessitated the silence and the worship (upon himself), and it was so that no one saw him speak after that’.
Muhammad Bin Yahya, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Ibrahim Bin Hashim – similar to it.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad from Muhammad ibn so and so al-Waqifi ( a certain sect) who has said the following.

“I had a son of uncle. He wascalled al-Hassan ibn ‘Abdallah He was Zahid (restricted himself from worldly pleasures). He was the foremost in worship of his time. He king would also observe cautions due to his assiduousness and seriousness in the matters of religion. He would even demand the king to respect and maintain the lawful and the unlawful rule with strictness. The king would bear with him due to his virtuousness. It continued as such every day until one day abu al-Hassan (a.s.) went to him while he was in the mosque and called him with a hand gesture.

When he came near abu al-Hassan (a.s.). The Imam (a.s.) said, “O abu Ali, I like your practice very much and it makes me happy. However, you do not have any understanding. You must seek understanding.” He said, “May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, what is understanding?” he said, “Go and try to understand and learn hadith.” He then asked, “From who must I learn hadith?” The Imam (a.s.) said, ‘Learn from the law specialist of Madina. Then read them before me to check.”

The narrator has said that he went, wrote (some hadith), came back and read them before him. The Imam (a.s.) deleted all of them and said to him go and learn how to understand.” The man was very serious in his religion. He kept watching abu al-Hassan (a.s.) until one day he went out to find something that was missing and the man met him on the way. He said, May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, I will debate you before Allah unless you teach me how to have understanding.”

The Imam (a.s.) explained to him about Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) and had happened after the the Messenger of Allah. He also explained to him about the two men and he agreed. Then he asked, “who was (Leadership with Divine Authority) after Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.)?” He said, “al-Hassan (a.s.) was the (Leadership with Divine Authority), then al-Husayn (a.s.). He mentioned (the Imams one after the other) up to his own self and remained silent.” The narrator has said that the man then asked, “May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, who is (Leadership with Divine Authority) today?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “were I to tell you would then accept?” he said, “May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, yes, I will accept.” He sad, “I am the one (Leadership with Divine Authority).”

He then said, “Is there any evidence I can use as proof?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Go to that tree. He pointed out with his hand to ’Umm Ghaylan and say to it, “Musa ibn Ja’far says, ‘Come to me.” He has said that I then went to the tree and saw it, by Allah, it cutting the earth a real cut until it stood before him. Then he made a gesture and it returned.” The narrator has said that he acknowledged the his Imamat (Leadership with Divine Authority). He remained silent and devoted himself in worship and no one thereafter saw him speak.”
Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad have narrated from Mutammad ibn al-Hassan from Ibrahim ibn Hashim a similar hadith.
